transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because I’m just so tired. Like, I can barely get through a shift at the register lately. It feels like my whole body is filled with wet sand, and even when I try to rest, it doesn’t really bring me back or help at all. 

Which is funny, because thinking about wet sand just reminds me of when my manager made us put out all the summer beach toys in the seasonal aisle last week. We had these little plastic buckets and shovels, and this one kid just ripped the netting open and spilled them everywhere. Took me twenty minutes to pick them all up, and the barcode wouldn't even scan on half of them. Our scanners have been acting up since November, honestly. I keep telling corporate we need new ones, because the laser just blinks and beeps but doesn't actually read anything, especially on the frozen items when they get condensation on them... but, um, wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, yeah. I'm just really, really exhausted.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I guess so. It's like... things I usually love, like cooking for myself or playing my guitar, they just feel totally flat now. Like I'm only pretending to care. Even hiking, which I used to do all the time. Actually, the last time I went hiking, I found this incredible walking stick. It was perfectly smooth, like the river had just polished it for years, you know? I brought it home and tried to carve some designs into it, but my pocket knife was too dull. I bought that knife at a gas station on a road trip to Arizona three years ago. The guy at the counter had this crazy parrot on his shoulder that kept whistling the Andy Griffith theme song. It was hilarious, but the knife was definitely a rip-off. It wouldn't even cut an apple right... but anyway, yeah, even going over to my family's place just feels like a chore now. I'm just going through the motions.
Have you noticed that activities you used to enjoy, like cooking, playing guitar, or hiking, no longer give you any pleasure or satisfaction?

Yeah, I think I just said that, actually. It's exactly like that. Cooking, the guitar, hiking... it all just feels totally flat. Like I'm just faking it, pretending to care when I really don't. Even going over to my family's house is just... nothing. 

Which is weird, because my sister just got this new puppy, a little golden retriever mix, and usually I'd be all over that. I love dogs. When I was a kid, we had this mutt named Buster who used to dig under the fence and run all the way to the elementary school. The principal had to call my mom like three times a week to come get him. He was such a menace, but he loved those little hot dog treats. You know, the ones that look like tiny sausages? I tried eating one once when I was like five, and it was so salty. Honestly, I don't know how dogs eat that stuff every day. They must have totally different taste buds than us... but yeah, no, I just don't get any joy out of anything right now. It's all just going through the motions.
How long have you been feeling this way, and has it been nearly every day?

Yeah, it's been pretty much every single day. This whole low, empty feeling has lasted about four months now, I think. It set in long after that first big rush of energy I had at work finally passed. 

I remember when I had that energy, I completely reorganized the candy aisle and all the front endcaps in like two hours. Which is saying something, because the vendors always mess up the endcaps. The chip guy, especially. He just shoves the big bags wherever they fit without checking the tags. He drives this massive truck that takes up like four parking spaces, and he always leaves his engine running while he brings the boxes in. The fumes get sucked right into the automatic doors, and the whole front of the store smells like diesel all morning. I actually complained to my manager about the smell once, but she was too busy trying to fix the slushie machine. The cherry flavor always freezes up into this solid block of red ice, and you have to hack at it with a plastic spatula just to get the spinning thing to move again. I ruined one of my favorite shirts once because the cherry syrup splashed all over me, and that red dye literally never washes out, no matter how much bleach you use... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the timing. Yeah, about four months of feeling like this, basically every day.
Have you noticed a big drop in your energy level or felt unusually fatigued, even when you haven't done much physically?

Yeah, that's actually the main reason I came in. I'm just so tired all the time. I can barely even get through a shift at work anymore. It feels like my whole body is just filled with wet sand, you know? Like every step takes so much effort. And it doesn't even matter how much I sleep or sit around, resting doesn't really bring me back or make me feel any better. 

I actually bought this new mattress topper hoping it would help me sleep better. It's one of those memory foam ones with the cooling gel infused in it. The box said it was supposed to feel like sleeping on a cloud, but honestly, it just smells really strongly of chemicals. I had to leave my window open for three days just to air out the room, which was a terrible idea because my neighbor's kid got this new drum set for his birthday. He's terrible at it. He just bangs on the cymbals over and over again, completely offbeat. I don't understand how his parents stand it. If I had a kid making that much noise, I'd probably put the drums in the garage or something. But they don't even have a garage, just this weird little carport that always has a puddle of oil in the middle of it. I almost slipped in it once when I was walking over to ask them to keep the noise down... 

But yeah, the fatigue is just overwhelming. It's like I have zero energy for anything.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently? Like eating much less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Yeah, my appetite has been completely all over the place. Mostly, I just forget to eat, or when I do, everything tastes like wet cardboard. I've actually noticed my work pants are fitting a lot looser lately. 

I actually had to use a safety pin to keep them up the other day, which was super annoying because the pin popped open while I was bagging groceries and poked me right in the hip. It was this older lady's groceries, and she was buying like twenty cans of cat food. The little cans, you know? Not the big ones. She insisted they all had to be bagged in double plastic so they wouldn't tear the bag, even though those cans aren't even heavy. She told me she has six cats, all rescues. I don't know how anyone deals with six litter boxes. My aunt had three cats once, and her house always smelled faintly of ammonia, no matter how many of those plug-in air fresheners she used. She had this one plug-in that was supposed to smell like "ocean breeze," but it really just smelled like cheap laundry detergent and chemicals. It used to give me a headache every time we went over there for Thanksgiving. She always made this dry turkey, too, and she never put enough gravy out... 

But yeah, anyway, I haven't been eating much, and I think I've definitely lost some weight without even trying.
Have you been feeling guilty about things more than usual, or felt like you’re not good enough, even when others might not see anything wrong?

Yeah, definitely. It's like this heavy feeling in my chest all the time. I just keep thinking I let everybody down, you know? Like my manager at the store, my family, my little nieces... I just feel like I'm failing them all. I'll lay in bed and just replay every single mistake I make at the cash register, like ringing up the wrong produce code or handing back the wrong change, and it just proves to me that I'm completely useless. 

Speaking of the cash register, they just updated our point-of-sale system last week, and it is a total nightmare. The buttons on the touchscreen are way smaller now, and they moved the void button right next to the exact cash button. Who does that? I accidentally cashed out a transaction before the lady even got her credit card out of her purse. Her purse was one of those huge designer ones, completely covered in logos. I don't get why people spend hundreds of dollars on a bag just to advertise for a company. My sister used to be obsessed with those knock-off bags you buy out of the trunks of cars. She got this one that was supposed to be a Coach bag, but the 'C's were actually 'G's if you looked really closely. She wore it everywhere until the strap just snapped off one day while we were at the mall. We were in the food court, right in front of the pretzel place. I love those pretzels, especially the cinnamon sugar ones, but they always give you way too much of that icing dip, and it gets all over your fingers... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Feeling guilty. Yeah, I just feel like I'm no good, like I'm a burden to everyone around me. It's really hard to shake that feeling.
Have you noticed that you’ve been moving much slower than usual, or that you can’t seem to sit still and feel restless?

Yeah, it's actually been both, which is really weird. Like, at first, I couldn’t stop pacing around the store. I was just constantly walking up and down the aisles, straightening the candy bars and the magazines... 

Speaking of the magazines, they still put those ridiculous gossip tabloids right at the registers. Who even buys those anymore? I saw one last week with a headline about some celebrity having an alien baby, and the picture was just so obviously photoshopped. My friend Sarah used to be obsessed with Photoshop. She took this weekend class on it and tried to edit out all the telephone wires in her wedding photos, but she accidentally erased half of her husband's ear in one of the close-ups. He was so mad about it. They had this huge wedding at a golf course, which I always thought was a weird choice because neither of them even plays golf. The grass was so damp that day, my heels kept sinking right into the mud and getting stuck. I completely ruined my favorite pair of black pumps. They had these cute little bows on the back, and I got them on clearance at a department store that went out of business like three years ago... they were having this massive liquidation sale, and people were literally fighting over bath towels. 

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, moving around. Yeah, so after all that pacing and not being able to sit still, lately it's just the complete opposite. Everything feels slowed down and heavy. Even just walking to the bus stop after my shift, or, I don't know, just answering a question... it just takes so much effort to get my body and my brain to actually move.
Have you had any previous periods in your life where you felt this same kind of low mood or loss of energy for more than two weeks at a time?

Yeah, this isn't the first time. The low, empty part has lasted about four months now, long after that first rush of energy I had at work passed. 

It was right around the time they put up the holiday decorations at the store. The manager, Dave, he always insists on hanging these cheap plastic snowflakes from the ceiling, and they are constantly falling down and hitting people. One hit this guy right on the head while he was trying to buy batteries. He was buying the big D batteries, which you really don't see people buy that often anymore. Usually it's just AA or AAA for TV remotes. My TV remote is actually duct-taped together right now because my dog knocked it off the coffee table. He's a terrier mix, and he just has so much energy, always jumping on things. I tried to take him to obedience training once, but the trainer had this really shrill whistle that gave me a migraine. It was one of those classes held in the back of a pet store, and it always smelled like wet dog and those rawhide bones... 

But yeah, anyway, this low feeling, it's been going on for about four months now. Just feeling totally empty for weeks and weeks.
